generation.explanation: At height z above the base, the cone’s radius is R(1 − z/h), so its horizontal slice has area πR²(1 − z/h)². The cylinder’s slices all have area πR². Adding the slices over the full height gives the cone a volume of πR²h/3—exactly one third of the cylinder’s. Move the slider to compare their cross-sections.
